genetic factors explain the majority of the variation of FE(NO) in humans and the covariance between FE(NO) levels of twins and the elasticity function of the arteries is explained entirely by genetic effects.
the genetic influence on FE(NO) is 58% and the genetic influence on Aix(ao), the marker of elasticity of large arteries is 70%.

genetic influences account for a substantial proportion of the variation in fractional exhaled nitric oxides, and that genetic factors are also involved in the covariation between fractional exhaled nitrics oxides and the marker of arterial elasticity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and environmental influences on FE(NO) and its association with the elasticity function of the arteries.
the genetic architecture of FE(NO) in relation to atherosclerosis.
the genetic and environmental factors influencing the relationship between FE(NO) levels in healthy individuals and aortic augmentation index, an indicator of elasticity function of the arteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic effects are important in both the FE(NO) and the Aix(ao), but their relative contribution to the variation in these two phenotypes is quite different.

genetic effects account for a large proportion of the variance of FE(NO) but the genetic influence on FE(NO) is not the sole explanation for the association between FE(NO) levels, and the risk factors of atherogenesis.
FE(NO) is heritable, and the genetic effects account for a substantial part of the covariance between FE(NO) levels in the airways and the elasticity function of the aorta.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FE(NO) is a complex trait influenced by genetic and non-genetic factors, with a modest genetic overlap with Aix(aO).

the heritability of FE(NO) is about 0.6, which is similar to the heritabilities reported for other lung functions, and that FE(NO) is a heritable trait that is genetically correlated with the marker of elasticity of arteries, Aix(a).
the genetic effects account for 58% of the variation in fractional exhaled nitric oxides and 58% of covariance between fractional exhaled nitrite oxides and aortic augmentation index.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic factors that affect FE(NO) and arterial stiffness are shared.
FE(NO) is a highly heritable trait and that the genetic effects that contribute to its expression overlap with the genetic factors involved in the expression levels of Aix(ao).
genetic effects account for the majority of variation in FE(NO), while the remaining part is explained by non-shared environmental factors.
